weekly_recap.previous_weekend:
Final score: Jason Carlton 98.78, Jay Nelson 87.48 — an 11.3-point margin that feels like a blowout compared to the rest of the league's photo finishes, but Jay still managed to make it look competitive right up until the math got involved.

This was the third meeting between these two, and Jason now leads their all-time series 2-0, which means Jay's trophy case for this particular rivalry remains as bare as his lineup card. Speaking of which — Jay, the trusted commissioner, ran Baker Mayfield out there for a putrid 4.08 points while Joe Flacco sat on his bench racking up 24.32 points. That's a 20.24-point gift-wrap of a loss, self-inflicted by the guy everyone trusts to run the league honestly. De'Von Achane's 17.6 points tried to drag Jay across the finish line but couldn't overcome that Mayfield-shaped anchor. Meanwhile Jason's Daniel Jones exploded for 23.18 points, burying Rico Dowdle's forgettable 5.4 and padding a card-ripping degenerate's win column yet again.
weekly_recap.honorable_mention: Brian Kleinhenz throttled Greg Wigton 116.06 to 88.64, a 27.42-point beatdown that's downright cruel considering Wigton actually leads their all-time series 2-1. That head-to-head advantage is officially decorative now. Jalen Hurts put up 25.36 points to power the rout, while Jake Ferguson delivered a goose egg for Wigton, the fantasy equivalent of showing up to a potluck with an empty crockpot. Kleinhenz, who's apparently more fun to trade with than to face — he's the guy always firing off those wildly lopsided proposals trying to fleece the league — proved this week he doesn't need help fleecing anyone, he can just outscore you outright. Wigton's two-year stretch of respectability takes a real gut-punch here.
weekly_recap.game_of_the_week:
Fresh series, zero history, which means neither of these guys can hide behind head-to-head mythology — just this season's tape, and it's not exactly flattering for the visitor.

Kevin Mallon's Salmation Nation sits ranked 6th at 4-4, averaging 111.84 points a game this season, riding a 50.0% playoff probability that feels generous for a team that can't crack triple digits reliably. Kevin logs 20 minutes of exercise daily and runs triathlons, which is more discipline than his roster shows on Sundays.

Greg Wigton's Invisible Hand is ranked 5th at 5-3, averaging 116.16 points a game this season, and sitting on a fat 90.0% playoff probability — the kind of number that lets a guy relax in the garage with a beer while everyone else sweats the standings. Both share an identical 24.5 power score, so the numbers say coin flip, but Greg's scoring edge and cushier playoff math suggest Kevin's cardio routine won't save him here.
